note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Benchmark design with two accuracy measures underlies the RQ1-RQ5 findings on question-type effects

nodes.name: Accuracy measures proposed
nodes.description: The study defines final selection (FS) accuracy, which scores only the final answer or selected option, and reasoning accuracy, which scores correctness of the reasoning steps (manually evaluated).

nodes.name: Benchmark design
nodes.description: Five LLMs (two closed-source, three open-source) are tested zero-shot on 300 GSM8K quantitative and 300 bAbI deductive problems (the latter with two added irrelevant facts), each formatted as short-answer, multiple-choice (with a 'Something else' option) and True/False questions.

nodes.name: FS accuracy differs by question type
nodes.description: There are more statistically significant differences in final selection accuracy across question types than in reasoning accuracy; e.g. on GSM8K300 SAQ beats 5-option MCQ in 8/15 cases and loses in 2/15.

nodes.name: Reasoning accuracy mostly unaffected
nodes.description: On GSM8K300, 80% of SAQ-vs-MCQ cases (12/15) and 70% of SAQ-vs-TFQ cases (7/10) show no significant reasoning-accuracy difference.

nodes.name: Reasoning and FS accuracy not correlated
nodes.description: Reasoning accuracy does not necessarily correlate with final selection accuracy.

nodes.name: Correct reasoning, wrong selection
nodes.description: LLMs sometimes reason correctly but select the wrong final answer (wrong option due to decimal/unit conversion, TFQ guessing before reasoning, or missing final selection), which makes SAQ performance better than MCQ/TFQ.

nodes.name: Models misunderstand 'Something else'
nodes.description: LLMs often fail to choose 'Something else' when appropriate, repeatedly recalculating to match a numeric option; Gemma and Llama do so in about 29% and 14% of MCQ outputs.

nodes.name: MCQ performance depends on design factors
nodes.description: MCQ performance varies with the position of the correct answer, the number of options and the wording of options.

nodes.name: TFQ performance depends on design factors
nodes.description: TFQ performance depends on instruction type, whether True or False is the correct answer, and word choices.

nodes.name: True answers reasoned better
nodes.description: LLMs mostly reason better on TFQs whose correct answer is 'True' than 'False'.

nodes.name: Question vs statement format
nodes.description: FS accuracy is worse for TFQs in question format than in statement format, except GPT-4o on bAbI300 and Gemma on GSM8K300.

nodes.name: Both skills must improve
nodes.description: Improving LLM performance on MCQs and TFQs requires improving both reasoning accuracy and the accuracy of selecting the final answer.

isolated_nodes.name: Models misselect options
isolated_nodes.description: Approximately 9% of Llama's MCQ outputs select an incorrect option after a valid calculation (Fig 3a).

isolated_nodes.name: Number of options effect varies
isolated_nodes.description: On GSM8K300, 5-option and 11-option MCQs show no significant difference for GPT-4o and the Llama models, but 5-option MCQs are better in 4 of 12 cases for the other models.

structural_reasoning: Benchmark design and two metrics feed the RQ1/RQ2 findings, the divergence between them motivates the error-pattern analysis, and factor analyses (RQ4/5) are separate.
